newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK 96/97 surplus forecast at HK$25.5 bln -- newpaper.
newsitem.headline: HK 96/97 surplus forecast at HK$25.5 bln -- newpaper.

text.p: A surge in stock market activity and property transactions could land Hong Kong with a budget surplus of more than HK$25.5 billion for the fiscal year ending March 31, 1997, the South China Morning Post estimated.

The newspaper's estimate, published on Thursday, less than a week before next Wednesday's budget speech, is more than 15 times the modest surplus of HK$1.6 billion previously forecast by the government.
About HK$16 billion is expected to come from stamp duties collected on stock and property transactions, up 160 percent over the previous fiscal year, the newspaper said.
The balance HK$9.5 billion will be from land revenues, the newspaper said.
Financial consultants are also expecting a healthy surplus.
Arthur Andersen estimated Hong Kong's surplus at HK$16 billion last week, while Price Waterhouse forecast it at HK$20 billion. -- HONG KONG NEWSROOM (852) 2843-6441
